title: Behold the Morning Sun
description: Behold the Morning Sun in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 19, part 2, headed “God's word most excellent; or, Sincerity and watchfulness”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the morn-ing sun Be-gins his glo-rious way; His beams thro' all the na-tions run, And life and light con-vey.

lines: His beams thro' all the nations run,
It calls dead sinners from their tombs,
And gives the blind their sight.
For ever sure thy promise, Lord,
O! may I never read in vain,
But find the path to heaven!
I hear thy word with love,
Send thy good Spirit from above
To guide me, lest I stray.
Yet, with a bold presumptuous mind,
And cleanse this guilty soul of mine,
While with my heart and tongue
Accept the worship and the song,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
